record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether benign fine-tuning changes harmful behavior and whether safety behavior is concentrated in a small set of units, using fine-tuning and neuron/channel pruning rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for benign fine-tuning on Alpaca, Dolly, and GSM8K and for pruning safety-, utility-, and redundant-unit groups. It also reports hidden-state cosine-distance probes, but not per-token KL or harmful-completion rates after a compliant prefill. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows. The paper’s freezing and PEFT comparisons are not extracted here; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own harmful-response rates after benign full fine-tuning (Alpaca, Dolly, GSM8K) on Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct, which bears on V2. It also reports ASR after structured pruning of about 1.3–2% 'safety-critical' neurons/channels, with utility-critical and redundant groups as controls, which bears on V5. Neither original source is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim that safety's atomic functional unit is the neuron. They attribute brittleness to fine-tuning converting safety-critical and complex units into utility units. Fine-tuning only redundant units is shown for general (not safety) alignment on Llama-7B.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unit attribution/pruning, benign downstream fine-tuning, and unit freezing; it does not reproduce the original few-example harmful/benign fine-tuning or per-token KL measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies by fine-tuning dataset and model; the authors report larger degradation for Llama 3 under Dolly than under Alpaca and weaker initial alignment for Mistral. Safety measurements also use different benchmarks and judges.

fits_no_version.finding: Hidden-state cosine-distance probes. Aligned (Alert-SFT) models' states for a harmful query sit closer to query+refusal tokens than to query+compliant tokens; unaligned (LIMA-SFT) models show the opposite. The difference holds across generation positions 1–10 and across layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety alignment changes which continuation trajectory (refuse vs comply) internal states favour for harmful queries.

fits_no_version.finding: Attribute-transfer analysis: during Dolly fine-tuning of Llama-2-7B-Chat, about 65.7% of SCUs become complex units and some CUs become utility units (Figs 5, 11, 13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning repurposes safety-critical units toward utility.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2026 (stated in the paper as published as a conference paper)
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported results. Safety evaluations rely in part on keyword matching and model judges; the probing results are shown as figures without extractable numerical values and use cosine distance rather than output-distribution KL. Some printed table values and parenthetical deltas do not align arithmetically.
record.rows_left_out: The freezing-policy and PEFT comparison results in Tables 2, 5, and 7–10, and the red-teaming fine-tuning tables 16–17, are omitted. They compare the paper’s mitigation methods or additional attack settings rather than adding the main benign fine-tuning or unit-pruning results recorded here. The 60-row limit was not reached.

untested.parts: No data-size sweep and no comparison of ordinary versus selected benign subsets. Only full datasets were used, with one training recipe per dataset.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL. The cosine-distance probes use custom LIMA/Alert SFT models and do not measure positional concentration of the output distribution.
The text says appended compliant tokens can make aligned models unsafe, but reports no rate. There are no prefill, suffix or decoding experiments; GCG/AutoDAN/PAIR are run only after fine-tuning.
Localization is tested at neuron/channel level only, not weights or ranks. Only 7–8B models were tested.
The binary-decision account (SSAH) is proposed but not tested against data or objective choices.
No training to deepen safety beyond the first tokens; the non-superficial extension is only stated.

missing.what: Jailbreak ASR (GCG, AutoDAN, PAIR on HarmBench) after benign Alpaca/Dolly fine-tuning of Llama-2-7B-Chat, e.g. GCG 33.33%→62.91% after Dolly. Column headers say 'GSM8K Finetuned' but captions say Alpaca/Dolly.
Own Dolly PEFT results on Llama-2-7B-Chat (LoRA, LLaMA-Adapter, Prefix): HEx-PHI high-harm rate 0.3%→26.5–27.9%. The Alpaca PEFT cells are excerpted from Qi et al. and should not become rows.
Freezing SCU+CU only partly prevents safety loss; SCU alone is insufficient, and the effect levels off beyond ~9% CU. Effect is weak on Llama-3 and Mistral.

record.verdict_notes: Verdicts: V2 supports and V5 supports. V5 also gets limits_scope from the freezing results in the text, which no row captures. UCU/RU rows were re-stated as controls: the reader's limits_scope on V5, built from them, misread nulls as qualifications. Mistral starts weakly aligned (Llama-Guard ASR ~40%), so its V2 rises are from a high baseline. The SCU pruning ratio is chosen to maximize safety loss at stable utility, so the size of the SCU effect partly reflects selection. Safety ASR in pruning uses keyword matching on 100 AdvBench prompts with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples or sweep a few-to-a-few-hundred harmful examples.
It tests benign SFT on named datasets, not a data-size sweep or a comparison of ordinary and carefully selected benign subsets.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement is reported.
No harmful-completion rates after compliant prefilling, suffix attacks, or decoding changes are reported.
The study tests neuron/channel pruning, not localization to a small set of weights or ranks, and does not establish universal localization across models.
The proposed account of safety alignment as a binary decision process is not tested by comparing data or training objectives for their effect on shallowness.
The study does not train safety to persist across response positions or evaluate whether such deepening holds up.
